subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw add a native subagent-specific circuit breaker, and if so should it be default-off, default-on with conservative thresholds, or folded into a broader session/provider health design?
rationale: The requested behavior changes config schema, persistent runtime state, spawn admission, user-visible failure reporting, and operator recovery semantics, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Approve a bounded native subagent breaker
options.body: Add a conservative subagent health design with explicit failure taxonomy, scoped persistence, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override controls, and status surfacing.

options.title: Fold into broader session health
options.body: Track this as part of the open gateway/session-level circuit-breaker design so subagent, provider, and session retry storms share one operator model.

options.title: Defer to existing guards
options.body: Keep relying on provider cooldowns, tool-loop detection, timeout, and concurrency limits, and close or narrow subagent-specific breaker requests later.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded native subagent breaker
recommendation.body: Add a conservative subagent health design with explicit failure taxonomy, scoped persistence, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override controls, and status surfacing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent spawn and registry history makes this the best available routing candidate for choosing the product boundary before implementation.
